basic_details.scholarship_name: Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology (DGIST) Presidential International Graduate Fellowship
basic_details.offering_entity: Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology (DGIST) & Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT), South Korea
basic_details.host_institutions_covered: DGIST Main Campus (Dalseong-gun, Daegu, South Korea)
basic_details.major_restrictions: Department of Physics and Chemistry, Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Department of Robotics and Mechatronics Engineering, Department of Energy Science and Engineering, Department of Brain Sciences, and Department of New Biology.
basic_details.number_of_awards_total: ~80 to 120 international graduate fellowships awarded annually across departments
basic_details.number_of_awards_pakistan: Open internationally; typically 10 to 18 Pakistani researchers in robotics, energy, and computing appointed annually
basic_details.duration_of_scholarship: 4 semesters (2 years) for Master's; 8 semesters (4 years) for PhD; 10 semesters (5 years) for Combined MS/PhD
basic_details.monthly_stipend_amount: Combined tuition waiver and research assistantship: 100% full tuition fee covered plus monthly stipend of KRW 1,000,000 to 1,350,000 / month for Master's (~PKR 210,000 to 283,500 / month) and KRW 1,400,000 to 1,850,000 / month for PhD (~PKR 294,000 to 388,500 / month)

nationality_requirements: International applicants whose parents both hold non-Korean citizenship (Pakistan fully eligible)
eligibility_requirements.age_limit_notes: No statutory maximum age limit, though priority is given to young researchers with exceptional academic momentum.
eligibility_requirements.academic_qualifications: Recognized 16-year Bachelor's degree with minimum CGPA 3.20/4.00 for Master's; recognized 18-year Master's degree with minimum CGPA 3.20/4.00 for PhD from an HEC-recognized university.
eligibility_requirements.grading_conversion_notes: Minimum CGPA 3.20 / 4.00; competitive applicants at DGIST typically possess CGPA >= 3.50 / 4.00.
eligibility_requirements.subject_background_prerequisites: Robotics, mechatronics, electrical engineering, computer science, energy science, brain sciences, physics, chemistry, or biological sciences.
eligibility_requirements.current_education_status: Graduated or final-year undergraduate/master's students completing degree requirements before semester start.
eligibility_requirements.work_experience_notes: Prior scientific publications in robotics, neuroscience, energy, or computing journals provide a substantial competitive edge.
eligibility_requirements.language_notes: IELTS Academic minimum 6.5, TOEFL iBT minimum 79, TOEIC 750+, or official English Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate from an accredited university.
eligibility_requirements.other_language_requirements: Korean language proficiency is not required; all graduate lectures, research, and dissertations are conducted in English.
eligibility_requirements.gender_specific_requirements: Open equally to all qualified applicants.
eligibility_requirements.special_eligibility_categories: All admitted international graduate students receive the DGIST Fellowship and research assistantship automatically upon admission.
eligibility_requirements.previous_scholarship_restrictions: Cannot hold another parallel government fellowship covering identical living and tuition benefits.

tuition_fee.details: 100% full tuition fee waiver covering all standard degree semesters at DGIST.

admission_application_fee.details: Online application fee of USD 50 (or KRW 50,000) paid via credit card on the DGIST admissions portal.

accommodation.details: On-campus international graduate dormitory housing in Daegu (twin rooms approx. KRW 120,000 to 180,000 / month), paid easily from living stipend.

monthly_stipend.details: Combined institutional stipend and laboratory research assistantship: KRW 1,000,000 to 1,350,000 / month for Master's; KRW 1,400,000 to 1,850,000 / month for PhD.

airfare.details: International travel between Pakistan and Daegu/Busan/Seoul is self-funded.

visa_fee.details: South Korean D-2 Student Visa fee paid directly to the Korean Embassy in Islamabad.

health_insurance.details: Mandatory enrollment in Korea National Health Insurance Service (NHIS); subsidized monthly premium (approx. KRW 70,000 / month) paid from stipend.

food_allowance.details: Subsidized on-campus student cafeterias across DGIST campus; meals cost KRW 4,000 to 6,000.

books_and_materials_allowance.details: Full access to DGIST Academic Information Center, core research instrumentation facilities, and brain-machine interface laboratories.
books_and_materials_allowance.amount: 100% covered robotics and brain science lab access

research_funding_conference_grant.details: Laboratory research grants cover international conference registration, travel, and accommodation for accepted papers.

travel_transit_allowance.details: Free campus shuttle buses connecting DGIST campus to Daegu metro lines and Dongdaegu KTX Station.
travel_transit_allowance.amount: Free campus shuttle & subsidized KTX access

university_and_program_options.single_or_multiple_universities: Single South Korea national research institute (DGIST, Daegu).
participating_institutions: Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology (DGIST Campus, Dalseong-gun, Daegu, South Korea)
university_and_program_options.university_rankings_scope: One of South Korea's four elite public S&T institutes (along with KAIST, GIST, and UNIST); renowned for robotics, brain-computer interfaces, and energy science.
available_majors: Master's / PhD in Department of Robotics and Mechatronics Engineering
Master's / PhD in Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Master's / PhD in Department of Energy Science and Engineering
Master's / PhD in Department of Brain Sciences
Master's / PhD in Department of Physics and Chemistry
Master's / PhD in Department of New Biology
university_and_program_options.program_duration: Master's: 2 years; PhD: 4 years; Combined MS/PhD: 5 years
university_and_program_options.admission_requirements_summary: Bachelor's / Master's degree with CGPA >= 3.20/4.00, academic transcripts, statement of purpose, two recommendation letters, English test score (IELTS 6.5+ / TOEFL 79+ / MOI), and CV.
university_and_program_options.easiest_hardest_institutions_guidance: Department of Robotics and Mechatronics Engineering and Brain Sciences are national flagships; establishing professor contact before applying is strongly recommended.
university_and_program_options.strategic_program_match_advice: Focus research proposals on autonomous systems, brain-machine interfaces, or next-generation energy harvesting where DGIST holds dedicated national research grants.

application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register on the DGIST admissions portal, complete online application form, upload personal statement and transcripts, pay USD 50 fee, and dispatch certified physical documents to DGIST Admissions Office.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Contact prospective DGIST professors in target research areas with CV and research interests (July-August for Spring / December-January for Fall).
Step 2: Register on DGIST Graduate Admissions Online System during open intake.
Step 3: Complete online application, upload documents, and pay USD 50 fee.
Step 4: Register two academic recommenders who submit evaluation letters online.
Step 5: Send certified hard-copy documents (degrees, transcripts, apostille/attestation) via DHL to DGIST Admissions Office in Daegu.
Step 6: Departmental faculty committee reviews dossiers and conducts virtual technical interviews.
Step 7: Final admission and scholarship award results announced online.
Step 8: Obtain Certificate of Admission (CoA), apply for South Korean D-2 visa, and arrive in Daegu.
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: Integrated Institutional Route: Admission and scholarship funding are decided together based on departmental faculty recommendation.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Submitted online by two academic recommenders via confidential portal links.
application_process_roadmap.personal_statement_prompts: Personal Statement and Study Plan (prescribed DGIST format) describing motivation, research experiences, scholarly interests, and post-graduation goals.
application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Structured research plan detailing proposed technical investigations, methodologies, and alignment with target DGIST laboratories.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Academic research CV detailing education, laboratory proficiencies, software skills, and publication history.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: Online technical interview via Zoom conducted by prospective supervisor and departmental faculty panel.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: IELTS Academic 6.5+, TOEFL iBT 79+, TOEIC 750+, or English Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate accepted.
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: HEC and MoFA Pakistan attestations required, followed by Korean Embassy consular legalization in Islamabad or Apostille.
application_process_roadmap.translation_requirements: Certified English or Korean translation for all non-English/non-Korean documents.
application_process_roadmap.final_submission_method: Dual submission: Online portal application followed by mandatory postal dispatch of certified physical dossier to DGIST.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Complete Bachelor's / Master's degree certificates and transcripts with CGPA >= 3.20/4.00.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Attested by HEC, MoFA, and consular legalized by Korean Embassy Islamabad.

important_dates_timeline.document_submission_deadline: October 1 / April 1 (Hard copy postal arrival in Daegu)
important_dates_timeline.annual_cycle_notes: Bi-annual intake: Spring semester starts in March, Fall semester starts in September.

selection_process_and_weights.academic_weight: 35% (Prior CGPA, academic rigor in engineering/science, university standing)
selection_process_and_weights.research_experience_weight: 40% (Technical research capability, publications, programming skills, research proposal)
selection_process_and_weights.personal_statement_weight: 5% (Clarity of vision and alignment with DGIST research priorities)
selection_process_and_weights.selection_panel_composition: DGIST Departmental Admissions Committee, School Graduate Deans, and Admissions Board.
selection_process_and_weights.evaluation_methodology: Rigorous holistic evaluation assessing mathematical ability, research productivity, experimental aptitude, and alignment with faculty laboratories.

competitiveness_profile.total_annual_applicants: ~1,200 to 1,600 international applicants across both intakes
competitiveness_profile.total_scholarships_awarded: ~80 to 120 fully funded international awards annually
competitiveness_profile.acceptance_rate_pakistan: ~14.0% to 18.0% for applicants with strong research profiles and CGPA >= 3.45
competitiveness_profile.typical_successful_applicant_gpa: Undergraduate/Master's CGPA >= 3.45 / 4.00, accompanied by strong programming skills or publications
competitiveness_profile.typical_academic_and_research_profile: Graduates with solid records in robotics, mechatronics, computing, or energy science, documented laboratory experience, and professor alignment.
competitiveness_profile.common_backgrounds_of_winners: Graduates from top Pakistani universities (NUST, FAST-NUCES, UET Lahore, GIKI, PIEAS, COMSATS, Quaid-i-Azam).
competitiveness_profile.high_representation_countries: Pakistan, Vietnam, China, India, Indonesia, Turkey, Iran, Russia.

fake_websites_and_scams: Only apply through official portal dgist.ac.kr.
DGIST does not work with third-party agents; all applications must be submitted directly by the candidate.
red_flags_and_warnings.application_fee_warning: Application fee of USD 50 is paid directly through the secure DGIST online portal.
red_flags_and_warnings.agent_and_intermediary_warnings: Applications prepared by commercial agents are rejected; authentic personal statements and research experience are essential.
hidden_costs_breakdown: NADRA FRC and document attestations (HEC, MoFA, Korean Embassy): ~PKR 35,000 to 50,000.
DHL document courier to South Korea: ~PKR 12,000.
Initial living deposit before first stipend payment: ~KRW 500,000 (~PKR 105,000).
misleading_claims_debunked: Myth: Korean TOPIK certificate is needed. Reality: 100% of graduate education at DGIST is conducted in English.
Myth: Flights are included. Reality: Airfare to South Korea is self-funded by the student.
official_vs_unofficial_discrepancies: Unofficial sites claim DGIST requires GRE; GRE is optional and not mandatory for international graduate admissions.

scholarship_obligations_and_terms.minimum_gpa_maintenance: Maintain minimum semester GPA of 3.00 out of 4.30 to retain the fellowship and tuition waiver each semester.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.attendance_requirements: Full-time physical research presence at DGIST campus; daily participation in laboratory research activities.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.academic_progress_monitoring: Semi-annual academic progress review evaluated by research advisor.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.work_restrictions_during_study: Off-campus employment is restricted under Korean immigration law; part-time work requires permission from immigration and university.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.home_country_return_obligation: None; graduates are eligible for Korean D-10 job seeker visas or E-7 professional engineering visas upon graduation.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.service_obligations_or_bonds: Zero service bond or repayment obligation.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.repayment_clawback_conditions: Tuition waiver is cancelled if semester GPA drops below 3.00 or if student is dismissed for disciplinary infractions.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_major: Major change requires approval from current advisor, new advisor, and department heads.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.extension_policy: Extensions beyond standard 4 semesters (Master's) or 8 semesters (PhD) are generally not covered by the scholarship.
